learningObjective: Diagnose why per-tensor MinMax INT8 activation quantization collapses accuracy on a Transformer layer with heavy-tail activation outliers.

canonicalClaims.claim: In LLMs, a small subset of activation channels carry very large-magnitude outliers; per-tensor MinMax calibration lets these outliers dominate the scale, starving the bulk distribution of quantization resolution. Mitigations include finer quantization granularity (per-channel/per-token where feasible) or techniques that migrate outlier magnitude to weights (SmoothQuant) or protect salient channels (AWQ).
conditions: The activation distribution has heavy tails concentrated in a small fraction of channels.
nonImplications: Does not imply per-channel activation quantization is always feasible.
Does not imply INT8 is unusable for LLMs — outlier-aware methods restore accuracy.

misconceptions.claim: INT8 GEMM cannot represent LLM activations; only FP16 works.
misconceptions.whyWrong: With appropriate outlier-aware calibration (SmoothQuant, AWQ, per-token quant), INT8 achieves near-FP16 accuracy on LLMs.

misconceptions.claim: The failure is a bug in the calibration code; a correct MinMax implementation handles outliers automatically.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Correct MinMax faithfully takes the observed extremes; the method itself is outlier-sensitive by definition.

misconceptions.claim: MinMax is the recommended calibration for LLM activations.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Percentile or outlier-migration methods are recommended for LLMs; MinMax is often the worst choice for outlier-heavy activations.

misconceptions.claim: Per-channel activation quantization solves outlier issues at zero cost.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Per-channel activation quant complicates GEMM (per-channel activation scale requires special kernel support) and is not free; hence the appeal of SmoothQuant, which keeps per-tensor activation quant.

implementationFacts: LLM.int8 identifies outlier channels via magnitude threshold and keeps them in FP16.
SmoothQuant introduces a per-channel diagonal scaling that migrates outlier magnitude from activations to weights.
AWQ protects the top ~1% salient channels via per-channel scaling and clipping.
performanceScenarios: GPT-3 175B: naive per-tensor INT8 loses several perplexity points; SmoothQuant recovers within 0.1 perplexity of FP16.
